dish_name: Gnocchi with Brown Butter and Sage
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat.
Pick the leaves off 2 or 3 sprigs of sage.

Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the sage leaves and cook for about 2 minutes, until the butter turns light brown and smells nutty. Transfer the butter and sage to a small bowl. Watch it closely, since brown butter can burn quickly.
Add the gnocchi to the boiling water and cook until they float, about 2 minutes. Scoop out 1/4 cup of the cooking water, then drain the gnocchi well.

Heat the oil in the same skillet over medium-high heat. Add the gnocchi in a single layer, working in two batches if they don't fit. Leave them alone for 5 to 6 minutes, until the underside is golden.
Pour the brown butter and sage back into the skillet along with the cooking water. Toss with the gnocchi for 1 to 2 minutes, until the butter coats them.
Season with 1/4 tsp pepper and a pinch of salt. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the Parmesan on top.
method_notes: Spend With Pennies (the lead, 4.92 from 25) boils the gnocchi, browns the butter with sage, then pan-fries the gnocchi until golden before tossing everything together with Parmesan. Lena's Kitchen Blog skips the pan-frying and just tosses boiled gnocchi in the butter, and Foodess loosens the butter with stock. I use a splash of the gnocchi cooking water to turn the butter into a sauce, with no new ingredients. Refrigerated gnocchi crisps better than the shelf-stable kind.
